taxonomy_mapping_dispositions.reason: The warning control reportedly became operative and identified generated content as outside guidelines, yet the harmful output remained visible to an eleven-year-old. In the evidenced child-safety context, detection and warning did not provide the prevention or containment needed to make the control effect protective.

The platform displayed guideline warnings for harmful sexual, violent and self-harm content yet still showed the material. Child-facing protection is engaged, but whether the system knew this user's age and which distinct heightened-response duty was unmet beyond the already classified activated-warning insufficiency are unresolved.

old_assessment.coverage_note: The Washington Post's screenshot-based investigation supports severe child sexual-safety rights harm at S5 and severe psychological harm requiring family, pediatric and therapeutic intervention at S4. The child was reported to be doing well by late 2025, so no suicide, catastrophic self-harm or presumed permanent psychological injury is inferred. Rights and liberty remains the controlling S5 dimension.
